note.note:
History:
• Chief complaint: Burning/stinging pain with urination (dysuria) for the past 3 days.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Occasional mild lower abdominal “cramping” when voiding.  
  – Noted a small amount of blood in urine earlier today; urine malodorous.  
  – No urinary frequency, flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting, or fever.  
• Bowel habits normal; no diarrhoea.  
• Sexual history: Sexually active with one partner (boyfriend of 2 months); uses condoms. No prior STI screen. Last menstrual period ≈ 2-3 weeks ago. Denies likelihood of pregnancy but advised to test if concerned.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• Drug allergy: Clindamycin → swelling (likely angio-oedema).  
• Medications: None regular. Took “over-the-counter bicarbonate” recently (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• No known chronic kidney, bladder, or other major illnesses reported.  
• Family history: No pertinent urologic or gastrointestinal diseases reported.  
• Social: Non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially on weekends. Lives with friends near college; biology student.

Physical Examination:
• Teleconsultation—no hands-on exam performed.  
• Patient appears well, alert, and oriented on video.  
• Reported negatives: afebrile, no flank or back tenderness, no visible or reported rash/throat swelling.

Impression:
• Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

Management Plan:
• Antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim—one tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact dose/route not documented).  
• Hydration: Encourage liberal oral fluids; cranberry juice suggested.  
• Sexual activity: Advise abstaining until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
• Red-flag advice: Seek care if fever, flank/back pain, or general malaise develop (concern for pyelonephritis).  
• Follow-up: Contact clinic or return by end of week if no improvement or worsening.  
• Pregnancy: Obtain a home pregnancy test if any concern.

Patient Summary:
19-year-old woman with 3-day history of dysuria, trace hematuria, and mild suprapubic discomfort without systemic features. Presentation consistent with simple cystitis; empiric 3-day oral antibiotics initiated with supportive measures and clear safety-netting.

Key Takeaways:
1. Take the prescribed antibiotic twice daily for 3 days; finish the full course.  
2. Drink plenty of water/fluids; cranberry juice may help.  
3. Call or return immediately if fever, back pain, or worsening symptoms occur.

Next Steps:
• Start antibiotics today.  
• Perform home pregnancy test if menses late or pregnancy concern arises.  
• Re-evaluate in clinic/telehealth if symptoms persist beyond the course or any red-flag signs appear.
